page: Amazon Web Services c6in.32xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processors, the instance delivers 128 dedicated virtual cores across 64 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory subsystem provides 256 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a 2 GB per vCPU ratio typical of compute-intensive profiles. Hardware acceleration support includes AVX-512 vector extensions with Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI) alongside accelerated cryptographic instruction sets like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Network throughput is a primary capability of the c6in series, featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps. The instance provides no bundled local NVMe storage, meaning all data persistence relies on network-attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) or external storage volumes. The lack of integrated storage reduces local drive maintenance overhead but necessitates sufficient EBS bandwidth allocation for I/O-intensive configurations.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallelized processing power, placing the instance in the top tier for multi-core compute metrics. The system achieved a PassMark CPU score of 86,862.87, with extended instructions measuring 107,468.03 and cryptographic throughput reaching 111,311.49. In synthetic multi-core stress testing, it registered 123,824.26 on stress-ng and 16,439.0 in Geekbench multi-core, complemented by an uncached read memory bandwidth of 332.31 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded metrics reflect average performance, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,696.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1,893.49.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio paired with high-bandwidth 200 Gbps networking positions this server for distributed computing workloads, Clang software compilation pipelines, large-scale Redis in-memory deployments, static web serving clusters, and multi-node batch analytics tasks that do not require local ephemeral scratch storage.

The hardware architecture incorporates AVX-512 with VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI acceleration, backed by a 200 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No local storage is included, requiring network-attached storage for persistence. Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-threaded execution, with a PassMark CPU score of 86,862.87 and top-quartile Geekbench multi-core results of 16,439.0, whereas single-core benchmark metrics remain in the middle tier. The hardware distribution fits high-throughput distributed compute jobs, network-intensive microservices, large-scale Redis deployments, CI/CD compilation, and scientific simulation workloads.
